_what: A recommended local title for every Subjects row with no catalog heading, and a recommended common subject code for every credit row with none, each with the level its source measured (Sam on #3655, 2026-11-21). A recommendation is for a person to accept or change; nothing reads it as a title or a mapping. A row whose courses are all noncredit is lined up with the standing noncredit subject title list by its dominant COCI noncredit category. Built by kb/_build_local_subject_recommendations.py; no clock is read.
_levels: High: the source's condition gave the catalog's own heading for 90% or more of the titled codes it was asked, each left out of its own vote. Medium: 60% or more. Low: below, or asked fewer than 20. Program titles are capped at Medium. A second source that agrees lifts a level one step; one that differs is listed under also and the row reads Low.

noncredit.note: Measured on the noncredit-only codes that hold a catalog heading (titles) or a common code from the subject map (codes), each left out of its own vote. A title condition right less than half the time is a guess: it stays measured here, used false, and gives no recommendation. The common code's answer key is the subject map, which reads a code without its credit or noncredit band (f-subject-map-ignores-credit-band-s698), so its share is a floor, and it reads Low.
